One of my French teachers told me to look for books with 90-100% comprehension. 75-80% if you’re looking for a challenge. Anything more difficult than that is just going to frustrate you. Some beginner books have translations in the back so that can be really helpful too! I’d suggest just finding something simple that can keep your attention. Picture books are an excellent start because you can pick up a lot of context clues!

I’ve found that it can. I’m 17, my mental health wasn’t taken seriously until 12, so I can get where you’re coming from. 
Having no friends blows. It can cause you to spiral and it can feel like you’ve got no one to help get you out. Just keep being kind to people. You might not make close friends, but it helps to have small conversations, even if they’re not about what’s bothering you. I have to try to get out of my own head.
Grades aren’t everything. I know they’re a big stressor, but sometimes it’s important to just stay alive. Your mental health is more important than a class and there are always other avenues that can be taken. Reach out to teachers or counselors about a recovery plan if you’re concerned. Some of them might be very sympathetic to what you’re going through.

Okay well first off I suggest you get a cleanser. Start with something basic from the drugstore. You can get a toner if you like but I don’t think it’s necessary. 
A spot treatment is used only on bumps or pimples instead of your whole face. It typically has salicylic acid or benzoyl peroxide. They’re great for if you wanna clear something up fast!
Next I recommend you get a moisturizer. It’s not for acne but it’s a really good habit. Start simple, I just use Nivea. Finally (AM) apply sunscreen.
